newsitem.title: USA: Riskier US junk bonds roar back, start-ups cited.
newsitem.headline: Riskier US junk bonds roar back, start-ups cited.

text.p: As another sign of exuberance in the U.S. high-yield corporate bond market, the calendar is once again crowding with aggressively stuctured offerings from start-up companies, market players said.

Merrill Lynch & Co is reviving a $125 million offering for Paging Network Do Brasil, a start-up Brazilian paging company, after postponing the offering in early April due to a downturn in the high-yield market, market sources said.
Morgan Stanely & Co is readying a $175 million deal for ITC DeltaCom Inc, a company building an integrated local telecommunications network in the U.S. Southeastern market.
Both deals guarantee interest payments in cash for the first three years by using a prefunded structure.

Conspicuously absent from the new-issue calendar are non-cash paying securities, such as zero coupon bonds or exchangeable PIK preferred stock, which had been popular financing vehicles for start-ups before the correction.

"Zeros are high-beta securities and tend to be very interest rate sensitive," said Les Levi, high-yield media and telecommunications analyst at Merrill Lynch. "A lot of market variables have recently improved, but there is still uncertainty about interest rates."

"When the market (for zeros) sold off pretty dramatically, it killed the performance of a handful of investment firms which had been big buyers of those securities" said the head of a high-yield bond syndicate desk at a major Wall Street firm.

"Those people got clobbered for playing and are not as receptive as they used to be," he said. "We'll probably have to wait for the recovery to last at least a month (before seeing the return of non-cash-paying securities) and that might depend on what the Fed does."
He added, "But if this market shows legs, watch out."
Despite such pockets of lingering wariness, market players said the appetite of junk bond investors for higher-yielding speculative securities has returned.

Recent deals cited are Radio One's offering of $75 million split-coupon notes to yield 12 percent and GST Telecom's $265 million three-year prefunded note offering which was priced to yield 13.25 percent.

Another example is this week's Coleman Co refinancing that involved the sale of $470 million in two types of four-year zero coupon notes, yielding 11.125 percent and 12.875 percent, market players said.

Market players said the deal was helped by juicy yields on short-term zeros. They also cited a willingness of Coleman bondholders to buy into the new deal because the company will use proceeds to buy back bonds at a premium to accreted price.
Analysts said reasons for the change in investor behavior are massive inflows of new mutual fund money, a more benign underlying Treasury market and still-strong economy.

On Friday's new-issue calendar, AFC Enterprises is expected to issue $175 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, rated B3/B, via Goldman Sachs. Price talk for the deal is 10.25 percent to 10.50 percent.
Also, Windy Hill Pet Food Co is expected to issue $100 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, rated B3/B-, via Chase Securities. Price talk is 9.75 percent to 10 percent.
In the investment-grade sector, CIGNA may offer $300 million 10-year notes and $300 million in 30-year notes via Goldman today.
